features.rationale: In progress: actual explicit-VM ordinary/optional calls, contiguous chains and construction retain receivers, ordered arguments and original newTarget, dispatch native/AST functions, and release roots on errors. Argument spread uses actual synchronous iterators, with Array values and code-point String iterator prerequisites. Per-thread Object call/construct nesting is limited to 32 and argument lists to 65536 values. Original Test262 coverage, bytecode function creation and fresh performance evidence remain incomplete. Engine still uses AST; #291 remains open.

Actual explicit-VM get/set/delete, computed key coercion, optional members, strict failures and receivers have integration tests. Original whole Test262 programs remain unsupported by the bytecode frontend due to calls/functions/other syntax; no AST fallback is counted as VM pass. Property code is in progress, #288 remains open, and Engine still uses AST.

Public Engine/ScriptRecord use actual global object versus declarative records, preflight ordinary-global conflicts before creating bindings, preserve descriptors and strict initializer behavior, and compare shared binding state/errors with explicit bytecode APIs. Configurable existing property reuse permits lexical shadowing under ECMA-262 2026. Full class/eval/Annex B/exotic-global semantics and Engine backend integration remain incomplete; focused upstream results and directory audit are separate evidence.

features.reference: Explicit bytecode API: Environment records and declaration initialization
features.rationale: Global/function/block descriptors instantiate actual Environment records with var hoisting, lexical TDZ, const assignment checks and pre-RHS dynamic references. Eight pinned Test262 variants execute in both AST and VM. Slots currently map to named Environment operations. Function frame creation, calls/captures, Engine backend selection and Boa speed superiority remain incomplete (#291/#292/#307/#427).

Inline short strings, immutable shared long buffers and bounded lazy concatenation ropes preserve UTF-16 contents, equality/hash/order, Send/Sync, Symbol identity and Engine alias/slice behavior. Allocation budgets include final rope flattening. Rope depth is limited; balanced-rope asymptotics, identifier atomization and identity across real Engine GC remain incomplete (#415, #257).

features.reference: Runtime reachability and ownership; Engine integration
features.rationale: Ownership migration selected in docs/runtime-ownership.md. Public Engine keeps live handles/closures/prototypes usable, but the strict teardown probe still retains three cyclic cases after weak internal function self lookup and deferred prototype allocation. gc::Heap is a separate component; runtime collection, managed captures and precise roots remain unimplemented.

Public Engine UTF-16 indexing/slicing, primitive prototype reads, boxed strings, ordered JavaScript coercion and exceptions. Focused pinned Test262: 56 variants pass; complete six-directory audit records external builtin/harness failures separately. Not full String conformance or derived constructor support.
Legacy String.prototype.substr is not exposed (#454); core slice and substring do not imply this legacy API.

JavaScript generic array-like operations, ordered side effects, holes, safe-integer limits, primitive boxing and abrupt completions. Focused pinned Test262: 50 variants pass. Full four-directory audit: 69 files pass both variants; 20 fail due to missing external builtin/harness dependencies, not counted as passes. Other Array methods remain incomplete.

Preserves throw values across synchronous call/catch/finally and embedding boundaries; native language errors are catchable while InternalError remains an engine failure. Focused pinned Test262 suite: 14 variants. Promise reaction values, suspended generator handlers, Error constructor API completion, and bytecode handlers remain separate work.
UTF-16-aware lexical goals and literal families are covered.

Expression parsing and reference evaluation are covered. AST addition connects ordinary JavaScript objects to default-hint primitive conversion; 12 focused upstream variants pass. This does not establish full operator conformance or intrinsic/wrapper completion (#176).
Declarations, control flow, and abrupt completion are covered.
Functions, arrows, methods, construction, and class syntax are covered.
Static module syntax, linking, cycles, live bindings, and top-level await are covered.
Execution contexts, realms, and environment records are covered.
Suspension, await, promise reactions, and jobs are covered.
Fundamental reflection and Proxy invariants are covered.

Packed/holey/sparse storage preserves descriptors, holes, key order, prototype and Proxy operations, and partial numeric length shrink. Non-number ArraySetLength coercion remains incomplete (#450); this is not full Array conformance.
Array, buffers, typed views, Map/Set, and weak-key behavior are covered.
Core text, numeric, Date, and JSON behavior is covered.
Collector primitives exist, but JavaScript WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry intrinsics are not exposed.
SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics are not implemented.
HTML comments are opt-in for Script source only.
Legacy numeric and string escape forms retain strict-mode distinctions.
Web-legacy block-level function semantics are not enabled.
Legacy RegExp compile and static capture properties are absent.
Date.now and construction use an injected clock.
ModuleGraph uses an injected source resolver with deterministic caching.
Dynamic import parsing exists without an embedding loader hook.
Intl is an explicit unconfigured host boundary.
DOM, fetch, timers, and browser event loops are embedding concerns.
using/await using and DisposableStack are not implemented.
Iterator chunking helpers are not implemented.
Iterator includes and join helpers are not implemented.
Non-Stage-4 proposals are excluded until explicitly selected by an issue.
